1.title: Cohort composition, data availability, and prediction endpoints.
1.text: (a) Cancer-type distribution among patients with cancer-type annotations and clinical text; counts and percentages use the same cohort denominator. Other combines less frequent cancer types. (b) Major cancer-stage distribution among patients with a recognized stage (I-IV). (c) Cumulative cohort selection as successive data-availability criteria are applied; each box is a subset of the preceding box. Repeated counts indicate criteria without additional attrition. PRS, polygenic risk scores; somatic, somatic genomic features. (d) Numbers of available prediction endpoints in the mortality/metastasis, three-character ICD-10, four-character ICD-10, and PhecodeX schemes. Endpoint counts are not patient counts, and related endpoints across coding schemes are not mutually exclusive. Panel-specific denominators are shown in the artwork.

2.title: Discrimination and survival stratification using clinical text.
2.text: (a) Held-out Harrell's concordance index (C-index) for the base model, containing age, sex, and cancer type, versus the model additionally incorporating clinical-text embeddings. Each point represents an endpoint; the diagonal indicates equal discrimination. (b) Endpoint-level differences in C-index (text minus base), grouped by outcome scheme. Positive values favor the text model. Diamonds and bars indicate the median and interquartile range; violin densities are omitted for groups with fewer than ten endpoints. Endpoint counts are shown above each group. Endpoints are correlated, so these summaries are descriptive. (c,d) Kaplan-Meier estimates of overall survival from first treatment in the known-stage cohort, stratified by major cancer stage (c) or quartiles of the text-derived mortality-risk score (d). Quartiles are defined across this cohort, with Q1 the lowest and Q4 the highest risk. Shading denotes pointwise 95% confidence intervals. Displayed C-indices describe the corresponding stage or risk-score predictor. P values in c and d are from log-rank tests. ICD-10, International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision.

3.title: Relative predictive performance and joint associations across data modalities.
3.text: (a) Points indicate mean within-endpoint C-index ranks (1 = best); horizontal bars indicate interquartile ranges across endpoints. Ranking requires complete modality-performance results and is restricted to endpoints represented in the joint Cox analysis; its endpoint count may therefore be smaller than in the other panels. (b) Numbers of endpoints with a significant modality coefficient in the unpenalized joint Cox model. Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment is applied across modalities within each endpoint; significance is defined as false discovery rate below 0.05. (c) Distributions of joint Cox coefficients per one-standard-deviation increase in each modality's risk score. Positive coefficients indicate higher hazard conditional on the other modality scores. Points represent endpoints; diamonds and bars indicate the median and interquartile range. For display in c, coefficients outside 1.5 interquartile ranges of the first and third quartiles are omitted separately for each modality; displayed counts are reported. Panels b and c use the same joint-model endpoint set before display trimming. Endpoints are correlated; summaries across endpoints are descriptive. PRS, polygenic risk scores; met. burden, metastatic burden.

4.title: Mortality-risk dynamics and survival across cancer stages.
4.text: (a) Longitudinal text-derived mortality-risk scores standardized within each observation month; colors are truncated at z = -2.5 and +2.5. Rows represent patients and columns represent months. Up to 500 patients per dynamics group are displayed, with shown/full cohort sizes labeled. Falling, stable, and rising groups are ordered by mean fitted risk-score slope. (b) Kaplan-Meier overall survival by dynamics group, conditional on survival to the indicated landmark. (c) Dynamics-group proportions among patients with each recognized stage and an assigned group. (d) Conditional overall survival for stage I-II patients with rising risk versus stage IV patients with falling risk. Legend counts in d report patients in each comparison group after landmark eligibility filtering. In b and d, shading denotes pointwise 95% confidence intervals; survival estimates use delayed entry at the landmark. Panel denominators differ with trajectory, survival, and stage-data availability.
